title: Ethernet Addressing
markdown:
An Ethernet (MAC) address is 6 bytes = 12 hex digits = 48 bits, written
colon-separated, e.g. `06:01:02:01:2C:4B`.

{{viz:0}}

A 6-byte address (Byte 1 through Byte 6) is shown as six boxes. The
least significant bit of **Byte 1** (the rightmost bit, marked with a
dot) determines the address type: `0` = unicast, `1` = multicast.

> **Note:** The least significant bit of the first byte defines the
> type of address. If the bit is 0, the address is unicast; otherwise,
> it is multicast.

> **Note:** The broadcast destination address is a special case of the
> multicast address in which all bits are 1s.

{{viz:1}}
